items.ai_summary: Security researchers have found vulnerabilities in robot vacuums with cameras that could allow hackers to access the devices. This poses a risk of privacy invasion and unauthorized control. Buyers should check for software updates or manufacturer advisories to address the issue.

items.title: Security flaw lets engineer control 7,000 internet-connected robots - NewsBytes
items.body: Security flaw lets engineer control 7,000 internet-connected robots  NewsBytes

items.title: CVE-2025-2894
items.body: The Go1 also known as "The World's First Intelligence Bionic Quadruped Robot Companion of Consumer Level," contains an undocumented backdoor that can enable the manufacturer, and anyone in possession of the correct API key, complete remote control over the affected robotic device using the CloudSail remote access service.
items.ai_summary: The Go1 quadruped robot has an undocumented backdoor that allows remote control through the CloudSail service if someone has the correct API key. This vulnerability means attackers could take over the robot without authorization, posing risks to privacy and safety for owners.
